codes.document_title: Code of Conduct for American Public Power Association Meetings
codes.notes: Event-focused code for meeting attendees. Prohibits unacceptable behavior at APPA meetings, with enforcement including expulsion.

codes.document_title: Business Partner Code of Ethics and Conduct
codes.notes: Covers fair dealing, anti-discrimination, confidentiality for APPA business partners. Prohibits manipulation, concealment, and misrepresentation.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics & Standards of Practice for Water Works Professionals
codes.notes: Establishes tenets guiding ethical conduct. Water Works Professionals are accountable for public health and safety. Emphasizes integrity and highest standards of business ethics.

Guides members in professional conduct; covers honesty, integrity, accurate representation of credentials, ethical marketing. Amended Jan 2020 to require WQA Glossary terminology. V3 updated Aug 2025.

codes.document_title: AGA Antitrust Compliance Guidelines and Procedures
codes.notes: Formal antitrust compliance and governance framework. Commits members to full compliance with laws and highest ethical standards. Includes AGA Antitrust Compliance Procedures for members.
14 principles of professional conduct. Approved by ANS Board of Directors Nov 17, 2022. Covers public safety, disclosure obligations, dignity/respect, diversity/inclusion, anti-bribery.

codes.organization: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
codes.notes: Applies to all IEEE members globally including electrical power engineers. Emphasizes public safety, integrity, responsible behavior, sustainable development, privacy protection. Last revised June 2020.

codes.organization: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
codes.notes: Companion to the Code of Ethics. Behavioral standards for IEEE members in professional activities, events, and interactions.

codes.document_title: NSPE Code of Ethics for Engineers
codes.notes: Six fundamental canons applicable to all engineers including utility/power engineers. Covers public safety, competence, truthfulness, faithful agency, anti-deception, honorable conduct. Includes Board of Ethical Review for case opinions.
Required agreement for all WNA member companies. Covers sustainability, safe/peaceful use of nuclear technology, transparency, IAEA safety standards, NPT compliance, and evidence-based policy.

codes.document_title: Establishing a Code of Ethics for Nuclear Operating Organizations
codes.notes: IAEA Nuclear Energy Series No. NG-T-1.2. Framework for nuclear operating organizations to establish ethics codes. Appendix A provides recommended minimum content. Applies from boardroom to working level.
Four fundamental principles: Accuracy & Rigour, Honesty & Integrity, Respect for Life/Law/Public Good, Responsible Leadership. Version 3, 2020. Members pledge to professionalism.

Adopted Oct 2009, reviewed May 2014. Covers integrity, environment/safety, competitor relationships, anti-bribery, product compliance, lobbying ethics. Members must adopt internal codes addressing antitrust, discrimination, workplace safety.

codes.organization: Chartered Institution of Water and Environmental Management (CIWEM)
codes.document_title: Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct
codes.notes: Binding on all Chartered CIWEM members. Covers fair/equitable/sustainable use of natural resources, lifelong learning, community service. Complaints process for violations. First created via 'Time for Change' document in 1999.

codes.organization: Chartered Institution of Building Services Engineers (CIBSE)
codes.notes: Covers building services engineering including utility systems. Updated Oct 2020. Principles: public safety, sustainability, equality/diversity, objectivity, anti-discrimination. Disciplinary process for violations.
Promotes highest standards of service in building industry. Members' paramount responsibility is to customers, community, and country. Adherence required for membership.

Adopted Dec 2000 by AGC of Washington Board of Trustees. 8 principles: honesty, respect, safety above profit, environmental stewardship, quality delivery, accountability, dispute resolution, organizational leadership. Voluntary and non-binding per antitrust regulations.

Originally approved Sept 24, 1971; reaffirmed June 2006 and March 2022. 8 provisions covering performance standards, honest pricing, professional cooperation, timely payments, safety leadership, fair compensation, industry training investment.

Binding on all AIC Members, CACs, and CPCs. Covers public interest, fair dealing, anti-deception, professional reputation protection, fair/unbiased advice, honesty, worker/public safety. Last modified Nov 2025.

Four foundational principles: Ethical Practice, Professional Excellence, Responsibility to Public, Client-Centered Practice. 10 core provisions. All CCMs/CACMs/CMITs must affirm adherence at renewal. Effective Jan 2021: minimum 1 ethics PDH for certification renewal.

Applies to all DBIA credential holders with enforcement and disciplinary action. Covers transparency, honesty, conflict of interest, anti-bribery, fair bidding, safety, confidentiality, IP protection. PDF dated April 2024.

International body for construction management professionals. Members must have full regard for public interest, demonstrate competence, act with integrity/honesty/trustworthiness, treat others with respect/fairness/equality. Recently relaunched after review. MOOC on ethics available.

UK's largest construction trade association (est. 1941). Requires written quotes/contracts, H&S compliance, regular client communication, guarantees/warranties. Members agree at joining and renewal. Reviewed by FMB Standards Committee.
Principles: Equality, Impartiality, Objectivity, disclosure of gifts/favours, national scope, consistency with CCA policies, confidentiality. PDF dated 2019.

Over a century old. Five core principles: honesty/integrity in business, professional competence, quality workmanship, objective/impartial advisory, industry skills training. Present across all Australian states (NSW, QLD, SA, WA, ACT).

Global professional body for built environment. Originally introduced 1971; current version Oct 2021. Covers honesty, integrity, transparency, conflict of interest management, public interest, fee disclosure. Applies to all members and RICS-regulated firms.

codes.document_title: Ethics Recommendations and Statement of Ethical Principles
codes.notes: Statement on ethical issues and code of good practice. Core principles for all professionals in construction law regardless of qualification. Working group under Peter Higgins. Principles: honesty, fairness, reliability, integrity, objectivity, accountability.

Originally adopted 1914; last wholesale update Oct 26, 2020 (first since 1974). Hierarchy of five stakeholder responsibilities: Society, Natural/Built Environment, Profession, Clients/Employers, Peers. Covers safety, sustainable development, anti-corruption, diversity. Ethics Hotline: 800-548-2723 x6151.

codes.document_title: NSPE Code of Ethics for Engineers
codes.notes: Six fundamental canons for all engineers including civil/heavy construction. Board of Ethical Review issues written opinions on ethical dilemmas. Foundational framework widely referenced in construction industry.

codes.document_title: ACEC Code of Ethics / Ethical Guidelines
codes.notes: For consulting engineers. Fundamental canons: public safety paramount, competence, truthfulness, faithful agency, conflict of interest disclosure, confidentiality. Direct impact on heavy civil engineering projects.

Six core areas: Responsibility to Society, Competence, Integrity, Impartiality, Fairness to Others, Corruption Prevention. Promotes Quality-Based Selection (QBS). October 2015 version. Global standard for consulting engineers.

codes.organization: Laborers' International Union of North America (LIUNA)
codes.notes: Applies to entire union structure and all members/officers. Covers democratic rights, health/welfare fund integrity, anti-racketeering, conflict of interest prohibitions, financial transparency. Inspector General enforcement.

codes.organization: Laborers' International Union of North America (LIUNA)
codes.notes: Nine member obligations: skills development, punctuality, job referral rules, attendance, following supervision, fair day's work, respect for property, dispute resolution procedures, workplace safety. Enforced via hiring hall referral penalties.

Referenced in IUOE bylaws and local union constitutions. Prohibits conduct discrediting the organization. Violations referenced in Section VI(A) barring eligibility for union office. Enforced through local union bylaws.

SPARQ values: Safety, Professionalism, Accountability, Relationships, Quality. Accepted by membership May 22, 2002. Members pledge punctuality, drug-free workplace, 8-for-8 work ethic, respect for property, no property destruction. Management must follow CBA and safety requirements.

Founding principle since NECA's establishment in 1901 by 49 contractors. Encourages active competition, sound ethical business practices, cooperation and good will among electrical contracting industry members.

Ten principles covering trade dignity, ethical advertising/pricing/installation, technological advancement, association participation, building code compliance, water/energy conservation. Published June 2018, last modified June 2019.

codes.organization: United Association of Plumbers and Steamfitters (UA)
codes.notes: Comprehensive standard for 395,000+ members. Three pillars: Excellence, Productivity, Safety. Member duties: punctuality, appropriate dress, zero disruptions, on-time completion. Contractor duties: safe environment, continued education, adequate staffing.

codes.organization: Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART)
codes.notes: 230,000 members. Code emphasizes honesty, trustworthiness, productivity, reliability. Anti-discrimination/harassment policy. Drug and alcohol abuse prevention. Public safety protections including hazardous materials handling.

codes.document_title: Model Code of Ethics for a Construction Subcontractor
codes.notes: Prepared for Sarbanes-Oxley compliance. 11 areas of ethical concern: competition, qualifications, standards of practice, conflicts of interest, public safety, suppliers, employees, public information, legal compliance, industry image, internal procedures.

Six 'I SHALL' commitments: excellent performance, honest business, fair treatment of employees/suppliers, knowledge sharing, quality masonry promotion, appreciation for MCAA objectives. Golden Rule creed. Constitution/Bylaws dated March 2024.

codes.organization: Mechanical Contractors Association of Canada (MCA Canada)
codes.document_title: MCA Canada Member Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Principles include honesty as foundation for business, fair profit, equal consideration for capital/management/employees/public, quest for knowledge, quality materials/workmanship, legal compliance, anti-fraud protections.

codes.organization: Painting and Decorating Contractors of America (PDCA/PCA)
codes.document_title: PDCA Code of Ethical Business Conduct
codes.notes: Membership requires agreement to code and proper licensing. Promotes ethical responsibility in business. Covers conduct toward customers, fellow contractors, employees, the association, and the public.
For merit shop and union insulation contractors, distributors, manufacturers serving commercial/mechanical/industrial markets. Members agree to highest customer service standards.

codes.document_title: ECA Code of Conduct and Code of Fair Trading
codes.notes: UK body. Code of Fair Trading ensures customers receive reliable service from qualified contractors. Members rigorously assessed before approval. Standards cover professionalism, safe/effective working procedures.
Also applicable to specialty engineering contractors. Six areas: Responsibility to Society, Competence, Integrity, Impartiality, Fairness, Corruption Prevention. Promotes Quality-Based Selection.

codes.document_title: CIOB Rules and Regulations of Professional Competence and Conduct
codes.notes: Also applicable to specialty trades management. Full regard for public interest, competence consistent with membership class, integrity to uphold dignity/standing of the Institute. Disciplinary process for violations.
